causal.assumptions_right: The 4.57 quoted anchor was not violently disproved: entry and exit prints were identical, so the book was not hit by an adverse catalyst-driven repricing. Exiting rather than adding kept the result bounded.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A calendar-linked Australian STIR expression can fail to reprice and still lose cash. Identical 4.57 prints do not imply a free option. The holding window's catalyst path was treated as a mechanism when the observed contract did not move.
causal.causal_divergence: The outcome was not caused by October 2026 AONIA repricing; the quoted move was 4.57 to 4.57. The divergence is a catalyst-repricing thesis versus an unchanged print whose residual cost is variance, not a catalyst firing for or against the long.
causal.future_implication: Do not open AONIA. Do not read a 4.57/4.57 scratch as confirmation or as a green light to re-enter Australian STIR. New risk requires a dated mechanism in an unblocked market, with explicit levels; otherwise remain flat.
causal.observed_reality: The position was closed long AONIA_2026-10, entry 4.57, exit 4.57, on 23 Sep. The quoted level did not reprice. The book is now flat. New Australia risk is blocked, so AONIA may not be reopened.
causal.original_belief: Long AONIA_2026-10 at 4.57 was a rates expression of a dated Australian policy or data mechanism that would reprice October 2026 AONIA away from 4.57 in the long's favor inside an identifiable event window, rather than a valuation view that could stay wrong with no clock.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same 4.57 information set and no observed repricing, not being long, or flattening once the event window failed to move the print, avoids the residual scratch. Extending the long would still have lacked a realized dated repricing at the last quoted level. Reopening AONIA repeats a blocked expression.

items.expression_assessment: Front-dated AONIA mapped the event, but an unchanged print shows the expression had no gap to close.
items.no_new_lesson: No new lesson: bounded ordinary variance around an unchanged 4.57 print and a residual scratch; the process remains sound. Do not overfit a rule from a non-repricing residual.
items.thesis_assessment: The dated-path claim was not confirmed: the print stayed at 4.57 and no repricing occurred.
items.timing_assessment: The holding window ended with the same quote as entry, so the clock expired without a catalyst print.
items.what_failed: A dated catalyst was treated as a mechanism when the contract never moved from 4.57.
items.what_worked: Exiting rather than adding kept the unchanged 4.57 print from becoming a larger residual.

causal.assumptions_right: A skip could print. Oil and 10Y could stay bid/hawkish through a hold. Mar STIR is first-order to the near funds path, not to term premium or presser tone.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Underweighted that the hold itself is enough to receive Mar27 even when the presser is hawkish. Underweighted the split between skip-tenor STIR and 10Y/oil. Treated the dovish-guidance clause as the binding skip condition, when the instrument was already bound by the hold.
causal.causal_divergence: Written invalidation was skip and dovish guidance. Skip occurred; dovish guidance did not. Mar SOFR still received because that contract prices the near policy path, which the hold reset, while hawkish presser and oil cleared in 10Y at 5.05. Exiting on the skip was instrument-correct even though the dovish clause did not fire. Staying in Mar would have been worse into 4.445 and better only if the same view had been booked in 10Y.
causal.future_implication: A hold is a Mar STIR receive event even when the presser is hawkish. Residual hawkish color and oil term premium belong in 10Y/belly, not in a skip-tenor STIR pay. Do not reopen Mar SOFR pay on Warsh, Bessent, or WTI 102.78 after the hold has printed.
causal.observed_reality: The Fed held on 28 Oct. Mar implieds were 4.52 at entry, 4.48 at exit the same day, and 4.445 in this freeze. Subsequent color was not dovish: Warsh hawkish on inflation, Bessent saying another hike is not necessarily a mistake, US10Y 5.05, WTI 102.78. The skip printed; dovish guidance did not; Mar SOFR still received.
causal.original_belief: Elevated Hormuz/oil would keep Mar27 SOFR implieds bid through the Oct FOMC unless the Committee skipped and guided dovishly enough to cut Dec hike odds. Invalidation was written as that compound: Hormuz fade without implieds above 4.52; bank-channel risk-off receive; or Oct skip with dovish guidance.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same 28 Oct hold print, waiting for Warsh/Bessent guidance would not have saved a Mar SOFR pay: implieds kept falling to 4.445 through hawkish color. Expressing the same oil/hawkish-inflation view in 10Y rather than Mar SOFR would have aligned with the post-skip tape. The error is where the view was booked, not a misread that the skip was dovish.

facts.invalidation: Hormuz headlines fade and crude backs off the 103.66/109.55 prints without SOFR_2027-03 moving above 4.52; CoreWeave-style stress jumps from non-bank into banks and forces a risk-off receive; or an Oct skip is delivered with dovish guidance that cuts Dec hike odds rather than preserving them.

items.no_new_lesson: The trade already listed Oct skip as an invalidation path and was closed into that print at 4.48. The post-exit hawkish Warsh/10Y/oil tape is not a process miss — it confirms Mar SOFR was the wrong book for that residual, because the contract kept receiving to 4.445. Executing the written skip-kill was sound; the leftover is bounded expression variance, not a new standing rule.
items.thesis_assessment: The oil-inflation-hike claim was not uniformly wrong: WTI 102.78, Brent 115.32, US10Y 5.05 (+6bp), hawkish Warsh on inflation, and Bessent’s line that another hike is not necessarily a mistake all survived the skip. What failed was the claim that Mar27 implieds were the vehicle for that thesis through an Oct hold. Belly and oil stayed hawkish; skip-tenor STIR received.
items.what_failed: The Mar27 pay did not keep implieds at or above 4.52 through the Oct meeting. The contract exited 4.48 on the hold date and is 4.445 in this freeze, so the Hormuz/hike-odds vehicle failed even though oil and 10Y did not fade.
